en: A sensation of whirling and loss of balance, caused by looking down from a great height or by disease affecting the inner ear.
A disordered or imbalanced state of mind or things analogous to physical vertigo; mental giddiness or dizziness.

note.ja: ラテン語 vertigo（回転）から。vert（回る）。→「めまい」。

en: The act of contemplating; being highly concentrated in thought; musing.
Holy meditation.

contemplation.ety: From Middle English contemplacioun, from Old French contemplation, from Latin contemplatio. By surface analysis, contemplate + -ion.

note.ja: con（共に）+ templ（神殿・観察の場）+ ation。じっと見つめること →「熟考・瞑想」。

en: Emerging; coming into view or into existence; nascent; new.
Arising unexpectedly, especially if also calling for immediate reaction.
A plant whose root system grows underwater, but whose shoot, leaves and flowers grow up and above the water.

emergent.ety: From Latin ēmergēns, present participle of ēmergō. The medical sense is a back-formation from emergency.

note.ja: e（外へ）+ merg（浸る）+ ent。水中から現れつつある →「新興の・現れ出る」。emergency（緊急事態）と同じ。

en: To bend or move (something) out of a given plane or direction, often the horizontal or vertical.
To slope.
A slope.
A portal of a subway tunnel.

en: To cut free.
To suffer disjunction; to be parted or separated.

sever.ety: From Middle English severen, from Old French sevrer, from Latin separāre (“to separate”), from se- (“apart”) + parāre (“provide, arrange”). Doublet of separate, from the past participle of that Latin verb.

ex.en: He severed himself from the party.
A foolish misunderstanding severed their long friendship.
ex.ja: つまらない誤解が彼らの長い友情を断ち切った。

note.ja: ラテン語 separare（分ける）から古フランス語を経た語。→「切断する・断つ」。separate と同語源。

en: That lives.
That has (or is believed to have) a spirit (anima) and/or some amount of consciousness and sentience, either being alive or supernaturall…
To impart motion or the appearance of motion to.
To give spirit or vigour to; to stimulate or enliven; to inspirit.

en: To turn aside or away.
To ward off, or prevent, the occurrence or effects of.

avert.ety: From Middle English averten, adverten, from Old French avertir (“turn, direct, avert; turn the attention, make aware”), from Latin āvertere, from ab + vertō (“to turn”).

ex.ja: 人間は誰しも死を避けられない。

ex.en: Skillful diplomacy helps to avert war.
ex.ja: 巧みな外交は戦争を避ける助けとなる。

note.ja: a（= ab 離れて）+ vert（向ける）。わきへ向ける →「（目を）そらす・（危険を）避ける」。

en: The act of reclaiming or the state of being reclaimed.
The recovery of a wasteland, or of flooded land so it can be cultivated.

reclamation.ety: Borrowed from Middle French réclamation, from Latin reclamatio. Equivalent to reclaim + -ation.

note.ja: re（元へ）+ clam（叫ぶ）+ ation。返せと叫ぶこと →「埋め立て・開墾・再生利用」。reclaim（取り戻す）。

en: Susceptible to superstitions.
Arising from or having the character of superstitions.

superstitious.ety: From Old French superstitieux, from Latin superstitiōsus, from superstitio + -ōsus. Cognate with Dutch superstitieus.

ex.en: She was superstitious, as the people of that period usually were.
ex.ja: その時代の人の常として彼女もまた迷信深かった。

note.ja: ラテン語 superstitio（上に立つこと→過度の畏れ）から。super（上に）+ stit（立つ）。→「迷信的な・迷信深い」。

en: Unwilling or unable to cooperate and associate normally with other people.
Antagonistic, hostile, or unfriendly toward others; menacing.
An antisocial individual.
